title: Securing Baby Capsule
content_markdown:
#### Indications

- Paediatric patient requiring transport

#### Contraindications

- Patient outside of capsule range.
Australian seat standards use *height and age* instead of weight. The Britax capsule is designed for *birth to approximately 4 yo*, governed by built-in height markers.

#### Precautions

- Babies under 6 months (or until they have independent head control) must be transported with the capsule fully reclined. If in doubt; 
- Check with the parent / care giver on their typical recline position, or
- It is better for a patient be reclined further than normal, rather than upright more than normal.

#### Equipment Required

- Essential: 
- Approved, ACTAS provided, baby capsule
- Stryker Stretrcher

#### Procedure

#### 1. Prepare the Capsule

Capsules are stored on stations in the upright position (Figure 1).

Figure 1

To fully recline the capsule:

- Locate the red recline latch (Figure 2) underneath the front of the capsule.

- Squeeze this red recline latch (Figure 3) and pull upward and towards you. You will feel a click. The capsule is now partially reclined.

- To fully recline the capsule: locate the blue release latch (Figure 4) which is found underneath the red recline latch. Use one hand to push the blue release latch and your other hand to squeeze the red recline latch. Continue lifting the capsule until it reaches the fully reclined position (Figure 5).

Figure 2

Figure 3

Figure 4

Figure 5

#### 2. Secure capsule to Stryker

- Ensure the stretcher is flat and all belts are clear. Place the capsule face the foot end of the stretcher and raise the backrest to meet the back of the capsule (Figures 6 and 7).

Figure 6

Figure 7

- Use the black anchoring strap (Figures 8 and 9) and loop it around the back of the stretcher. Pull the strap to tighten and remove any slack (Figures 10 and 11).

Figure 8

Figure 9

Figure 10

Figure 11

- Feed the stretcher waist belt through the yellow lap belt path on the capsule (Figure 12). Connect the buckle and tighten the belt while pushing down on the capsule to remove all slack (Figure 13).

Figure 12

Figure 13

- Feed the ankle belt from the stretcher through the blue rear facing path at the foot end of the capsule (Figures 14 and 15). Push down on the capsule while tightening the belt to remove all slack. Secure the belt in the blue lock-off clip on both sides of the capsule (Figure 16). 

Figure 14

Figure 15

Figure 16

Check for movement. If the capsule moves more than 2 cm side-to-side or front-to-back, retighten the belts.

#### 3. Adjust capsule

**Shoulder straps must be level with, or just above, the baby’s shoulders. They must NEVER sit below the shoulders.**

- To adjust the headrest/shoulder straps: lift the red headrest adjustment lever at the top of the capsule (Figure 17), then pull up or push down to adjust the height of the headrest/shoulder straps so they are level with, or just above, the baby’s shoulders. Release the red lever to lock in position. 
Figure 17

- The headrest and harness height can be adjusted while the baby remains in the capsule. Ensure no fabric becomes trapped or bunched behind the baby’s back.

- Loosen/lengthen the harness straps prior to placing baby in the capsule. Press and hold the black harness adjustment button and pull both shoulder straps upward to loosen the harness (Figures 18 and 19).

Figure 18

Figure 19

- Position the baby flat on their back with the buckle between the legs. Ensure the shoulder straps sit at the correct height before fastening the harness (Figures 20 and 21).

Figure 20

Figure 21

- To tighten the straps, remove slack from the lap straps by pulling the shoulder straps upward (Figure 22). Pull the harness adjustment strap (Figure 23) until the harness is firm and secure (Figure 24).

Figure 22

Figure 23

Figure 24

#### 4. Harness Fit Check

##### Harness Fit Check

**Pinch Test**

Attempt to pinch the harness webbing at the baby’s collarbone.

Correct fit (Figure 25):

- Fingers slide off the webbing
- Unable to pinch or fold the harness material

Too loose (Figure 26):

- Harness webbing can be pinched or folded

Figure 25

Figure 26

##### Harness Too Tight

**Flat Finger Test**

Place two flat fingers between the harness and the baby’s chest.

Correct fit (Figure 27):

- Two flat fingers fit comfortably under the harness

Too tight:

- Two flat fingers cannot fit beneath the harness
- Harness visibly digs into the shoulders- Arms are pulled into an unnatural position
Figure 27

#### Notes

##### Key Notes

- Babies under 6 months must be transported fully reclined
- Capsule faces the foot end of the stretcher
- Remove all slack from stretcher belts- Shoulder straps must be level with or above the baby’s shoulders- Complete the Final Safety Check before transport
##### Final Safety Check
Before Transport, confirm
- Capsule fully reclined
- Capsule facing foot end of stretcher- Anchoring strap attached and secure- Waist belt routed through yellow belt path- Ankle belt routed through blue rear-facing path- Lock-off clips secured- Harness straps at correct height- Harness passes pinch and flat finger tests- Baby positioned correctly with arms and legs free of straps
